title: Several Contenders Circle Tigers Starter Casey Mize Ahead of MLB Trade Deadline
excerpt: The former No. 1 overall pick, enjoying a career-best season with a 2.70 ERA, was scratched from his Friday start as Detroit weighs dealing him before Monday's deadline.
body:
• Tigers right-hander Casey Mize was scratched from his scheduled Friday start for non-injury reasons, a widely recognized precursor to a trade before Monday's August 3 deadline.
  • Mize is posting career-best numbers — a 2.70 ERA and 0.99 WHIP in 16 starts — making him one of the most attractive mid-rotation arms available.
  • The Cubs, Braves, Padres, Cardinals, Brewers, and Diamondbacks are among the teams linked to Mize, who will be a free agent after this season.
  • Unlike teammate Tarik Skubal, Mize's rental status means he would cost contenders far less in prospect capital.

Detroit Tigers right-hander Casey Mize is emerging as one of the most coveted pitching targets ahead of Monday's MLB trade deadline, with at least half a dozen contenders expressing interest in the 29-year-old starter.

The Tigers scratched Mize from his scheduled Friday start against the Kansas City Royals for non-injury reasons, a move widely interpreted as a precautionary step before a potential deal. Detroit sits 10 games under .500 at the All-Star break and appears poised to sell before the August 3 cutoff.

Career-Best Numbers

Mize, the No. 1 overall pick in the 2018 draft, is enjoying arguably the best season of his career. Through 16 starts, he has posted a 2.70 ERA and 0.99 WHIP with strong strikeout numbers. He has allowed two or fewer runs in 11 of his 15 completed starts.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=gTupnDPAg8k

"Where we are as a team makes that more simple to deal with. There are so many unknowns. We're in a 10-game sprint right now, and it takes tons of focus on what we're doing here and now."

— Casey Mize, on the trade speculation

ESPN's Jeff Passan and Kiley McDaniel pegged Mize's chance of being traded at 60 percent, calling his rest-of-season impact "high if it continues to click." They noted his four above-average pitches — fastball, cutter, sweeper, and splitter — all performing at or above average by runs value.

Suitor List Grows

The Chicago Cubs are among the most aggressive pursuers. USA Today reported that Chicago would ideally add three pitchers — a combination of starters and relievers — and has already held talks about Mize along with Robbie Ray, Clay Holmes, and Emerson Hancock.

The Atlanta Braves are another logical fit. With Spencer Schwellenbach recovering from elbow surgery and Spencer Strider still sidelined, Mize would provide stability behind ace Chris Sale. The Braves typically avoid blockbuster deadline trades, making Mize's lower price tag appealing.

The St. Louis Cardinals, San Diego Padres, Milwaukee Brewers, Arizona Diamondbacks, Tampa Bay Rays, and Toronto Blue Jays have also been identified as potential landing spots.

Rental Advantage

Mize will be a free agent after this season, which works in both directions. Contenders can add a proven mid-rotation arm without surrendering top-tier prospects, while the Tigers should receive a reasonable return without the pressure of maximizing value on a multi-year contract.

His $6.15 million salary is manageable for most contenders. The bigger question is health — Mize has twice hit the injured list this season with a strained groin, though his most recent starts suggest the issue is behind him.

A decision from Detroit could come as early as this weekend, with the Monday deadline looming.
